reason: Section 25 requires a person claiming compensation to deliver a written claim to the Minister with full particulars and the person's right and title to compensation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Written claim for injurious affection compensation

evidenceText: shall deliver to the Minister a written claim
full particulars
right and title to such compensation

proposedGroups.reason: The section contains one claim-delivery requirement for compensation claimants.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a compensation claimant must include in the written claim delivered to the Minister.

reason: Section 26 requires the Minister, when not agreeing with the claimant, to offer a reasonable compensation amount in writing and give notice that non-acceptance leads to Court of King's Bench submission under the Expropriation Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister's written compensation offer and notice

evidenceText: does not agree with the person claiming compensation
shall offer in writing
give notice in writing
submitted to The Court of King's Bench

proposedGroups.reason: The section is one procedural step after disagreement about compensation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what written offer and notice the Minister must give when compensation is not agreed.

reason: Section 27 requires the Minister to submit compensation to the Court of King's Bench for determination if the section 26 offer is not accepted.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court determination after compensation offer refused

evidenceText: offer of the Minister under section 26 is not accepted
shall submit the matter of compensation
for determination

proposedGroups.reason: The section states the next step when the Minister's compensation offer is not accepted.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what the Minister must do when a section 26 compensation offer is refused.

reason: Section 28 combines uncompensated highway-purpose removal and entry powers, a damage compensation exception for shore or bed materials, snow-fence powers, and a court-backed warrant process for resistance.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Removal, material, and snow-fence powers without compensation

evidenceText: without compensating the owner
may remove for highway purposes
may take and carry away
may enter upon any lands adjacent to a highway

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 28(1) lists the Minister or agent powers over materials, encroachments, shore or bed materials, fences, and snow fences, including the compensation exception for damage under paragraph (c).
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister or agent powers to remove materials or obstructions, use shore or bed materials, and handle fences or snow fences for highway purposes.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Warrant process for resistance to highway removal or demolition

evidenceText: resistance or opposition
may issue a warrant to the sheriff
shall make a return of the warrant

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 28(2) and 28(3) provide the judicial warrant and sheriff return process when removal or demolition under paragraph 28(1)(b) is resisted.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how resistance to authorized highway removal or demolition can be addressed through a court warrant and sheriff return.

reason: Section 29 authorizes the Minister to certify highway status and makes that certificate conclusive evidence.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister's certificate as conclusive highway evidence

evidenceText: may certify that any highway or portion thereof is a highway
certificate shall be conclusive evidence

proposedGroups.reason: The section contains one certification and evidentiary-effect rule.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the effect of the Minister's certificate that a highway or portion is a highway.

reason: Section 30 covers width presumptions and requirements for highways, Lieutenant-Governor in Council authority to allow narrower highways, and the centre-line rule for boundary doubts or disputes.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Highway width presumptions and minimum widths

evidenceText: deemed to have been laid out four rods in width
shall be at least 20 m in width
less than 20 m but not less than 10 m

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 30(1) to 30(3) address deemed width for existing highways, default width for new highways, and orders allowing narrower width.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the four-rod presumption, 20 m minimum, and 10 m lower limit for highway width.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Centre line for disputed highway boundaries

evidenceText: doubt or dispute as to the boundaries of a highway
centre line of the travelled portion

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 30(4) is a separate boundary rule based on the centre line of the travelled portion.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize how the centre line of a highway is determined when highway boundaries are in doubt or dispute.

reason: Section 31 authorizes Ministerial construction standards for roads and streets in specified local governments, exemptions where subdivision by-laws prescribe standards, and an offence for contravening applicable standards.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Construction standards for village, rural community, and regional municipality streets

evidenceText: may establish the standards
may exempt the village, rural community or regional municipality
commits an offence

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections together set standards, possible local exemption, and offence consequences.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how road or street construction standards apply in villages, rural communities, and regional municipalities and when contravention is an offence.

reason: Section 32 combines a historical vesting declaration for soil and freehold with a current proclamation mechanism releasing highways to local government jurisdiction and vesting Crown-owned soil and freehold in that local government.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Historical vesting of highway soil and freehold in abutting owners

evidenceText: title to the soil and freehold of highways
vested in the owners of lands abutting the highways

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 32(1) is a distinct vesting declaration concerning abutting owners and successors in title.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the declared vesting of soil and freehold of certain highways in abutting owners and their successors.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Proclamation releasing highways to local government control

evidenceText: cease to be under the control of the Minister
under the jurisdiction of the local government
vested in that local government

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 32(2) and 32(3) cover proclamation-based transfer of highway control and Crown-owned soil and freehold to the named local government.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a highway can cease to be under Ministerial control and how related Crown-owned soil and freehold vests in a local government.

reason: Section 33 covers discontinuance filing methods and effects, access protection before discontinuance, cessation of public passage rights, and ratification of earlier discontinuances.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recording and immediate effect of highway discontinuance

evidenceText: not required for use by the public
recording in the appropriate land registration office
ceases to be a highway

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 33(1) states when and how the Minister may discontinue a highway or road and the immediate result.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the recording methods and highway-status effect of discontinuing a highway or road.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Access protection and public rights after discontinuance

evidenceText: would isolate any property from a highway
adequate access to a highway is provided
all rights of the public to pass

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 33(2) and 33(3) address access safeguards and the cessation of public passage rights.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the adequate-access safeguard and the effect of discontinuance on public passage rights.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ratification of earlier highway discontinuances

evidenceText: prior to the coming into force of this section
ratified and confirmed

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 33(4) separately ratifies and confirms earlier discontinuances and applies the public-rights effect to them.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize how section 33 treats highway discontinuances made before the current section came into force.

reason: Section 34 authorizes the Minister to close highways by posted signs or notices, limit closure to vehicle classes, and makes operation on a closed highway an offence.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Posted highway closures and offence for operating on closed highway

evidenceText: may close temporarily, permanently or for a specified period of time
limit the closing
commits an offence

proposedGroups.reason: The current subsections together cover the closure authority, vehicle-class limitation, evidentiary effect of posted signs, and offence for operating on a closed highway.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how highway closures are posted and proved, how they may be limited by vehicle class, and when operation on a closed highway is an offence.

reason: Section 34.1 creates the permit mechanism for operating on a closed highway, including issuance, exemption from the closed-highway offence, cancellation or suspension, reinstatement, amendment, and renewal.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Permits to operate on closed highways

evidenceText: may issue a permit
Subsection 34(3) does not apply
may cancel or suspend
may amend or renew

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections form one permit regime for closed-highway operation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how permits authorize operation on closed highways and how they may be cancelled, suspended, reinstated, amended, or renewed.

reason: Section 35 states when roads constructed by others become highways and authorizes the Minister to accept roads or streets as highways despite the Community Planning Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ministerial certification accepting roads as highways

evidenceText: shall become a highway
until the Minister certifies
may accept a road or street as a highway

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections depend on Ministerial certification and designation amendment for road or street acceptance as a highway.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a road or street becomes a highway through Ministerial certification and designation amendment.

reason: Section 36 is a large height and weight restriction regime with definitions, imposition and proof of restrictions, offences and penalties, damage liability, special permits, and exemptions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Height and weight restriction definitions and posting
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 36(1) to 36(6) define key restriction terms and explain how restrictions are imposed, amended, cancelled, noticed, and proved.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions of height and weight restrictions and how Minister-posted restrictions take effect, are proved, and may be amended or cancelled.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Offences, penalties, and damage liability for excess height or weight
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 36(7) to 36(11) cover offences for exceeding restrictions, excess-weight penalties, and joint and several liability for resulting damage.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the offence, penalty, and damage-liability consequences of operating vehicles over height or weight restrictions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Special permits and exemptions from weight restrictions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 36(12) to 36(15) address special permits, their effect and liability limits, and exemptions for emergency or maintenance vehicles.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when special permits may authorize operation despite weight restrictions and which vehicles are exempt from bridge weight restrictions.
